title: Objective assessments of longitudinal outcome in Gilles de la Tourette's syndrome
design: Longitudinal childhood/adult video comparison; rater hypothesis-blind, age/timepoint blinding not established.
key_result: Objective improvement, but 90% retained tics.
uncertainty: Small tertiary cohort; attrition; short recordings.
inference_not_supported: Universal adult persistence rate or irreversible biology.
retrieval_status: Institutional-hosted original full text inspected; see analyses/remission/2026-10-09-harmonization.md.

title: Course of Tourette Syndrome and Comorbidities in a Large Prospective Clinical Study
design: Six-year prospective Danish clinic cohort.
key_result: Reported above-age-16 categories: 17.7% no tics; 59.5% minimal/mild. Original denominator unit not verified; do not assume unique follow-up participants.
uncertainty: Referral selection; attrition; outcome definition. Author thesis pools tic assessments and contains inconsistent table totals; reconstructed denominator provisional. Comorbidity 63%=92/146 DAWBA respondents.
inference_not_supported: Permanent remission or population-wide percentages.
retrieval_status: PubMed abstract plus investigator doctoral thesis inspected; original journal tables outstanding. See analyses/remission/2026-10-09-harmonization.md.

title: Long-term follow-up of an epidemiologically defined cohort of patients with Tourette syndrome
design: Prospective community-ascertained childhood cohort, later interviews.
key_result: Tic severity declined 59%; 44% essentially symptom-free.
uncertainty: Interview ascertainment and attrition.
inference_not_supported: Objective complete disappearance in 44%.
retrieval_status: PubMed abstract retrieved.

title: Sleep in Gilles de la Tourette's syndrome: disorder of arousal
design: Overnight polygraphy, accelerometry and video; untreated TS versus controls.
key_result: Motor tics observed in all sleep stages.
uncertainty: Small historical, age-mixed sample.
inference_not_supported: Universal sleep cessation or universal stage-specific frequency.
retrieval_status: PubMed and publisher abstracts retrieved.

title: Decreased sleep quality and increased sleep related movements in patients with Tourette's syndrome
design: Adult case-control video-polysomnography.
key_result: Tics across sleep stages; REM frequency exceeded non-REM.
uncertainty: Small observational sample; directionality unresolved.
inference_not_supported: Sleep abnormalities cause TS.
retrieval_status: PubMed abstract retrieved; PMC full-text access challenge.

title: Disturbed sleep in children with Tourette syndrome: a polysomnographic study
design: Unmedicated children without ADHD versus matched controls.
key_result: Sleep efficiency worsened; arousal-related movements increased.
uncertainty: Small selected sample.
inference_not_supported: Improving sleep cures or necessarily reduces tics.
retrieval_status: PubMed abstract retrieved.

title: Caudate volumes in childhood predict symptom severity in adults with Tourette syndrome
design: Childhood MRI and clinical follow-up averaging 7.5 years.
key_result: Smaller childhood caudate associated with worse later symptoms.
uncertainty: Small clinic cohort; medication and retention confounding.
inference_not_supported: Causal target or validated individual prognosis.
retrieval_status: PubMed abstract and indexed PMC discussion retrieved.

title: Increased GABA contributes to enhanced control over motor excitability in Tourette syndrome
design: Cross-sectional 7-T MRS with functional/neurophysiological measures.
key_result: Higher SMA GABA associated with lower excitability.
uncertainty: Small sample; MRS does not isolate synaptic mechanisms.
inference_not_supported: GABA elevation causes remission.
retrieval_status: Indexed PMC full-text passages retrieved.
n_note: Matched control group; exact control count not independently extracted from primary text.

title: Distinct cerebellar networks underpin clinical improvement in adolescent Tourette disorder
design: Longitudinal functional MRI, approximately 15 months.
key_result: Tic improvement correlated with frontal control-network connectivity changes.
uncertainty: Selected low/moderate severity; medication and suppression confounding.
inference_not_supported: Causal remission pathway or clinically validated biomarker.
retrieval_status: Publisher full text inspected.

title: Mispatterning and interneuron deficit in Tourette Syndrome Basal Ganglia Organoids
design: Donor-derived basal-ganglia organoid comparison.
key_result: Altered patterning and reduced interneuron differentiation.
uncertainty: Few donors; developmental model, not intact brain.
inference_not_supported: Universal lesion or established repair therapy.
retrieval_status: PMC full text inspected.

title: Interneuron Loss and Microglia Activation by Transcriptome Analyses in the Basal Ganglia of Tourette Disorder
design: Postmortem striatal single-nucleus RNA/ATAC sequencing.
key_result: Reduced interneurons with metabolic and microglial alterations.
uncertainty: Small persistent-adult sample; treatment and tissue confounding.
inference_not_supported: Immune activation initiates TS.
retrieval_status: Published abstract verified via author institution; indexed full-text passages.

title: Behavior Therapy for Children with Tourette Disorder: A Randomized Controlled Trial
design: Assessor-blinded CBIT versus supportive therapy/education.
key_result: Clinical improvement: 52.5% versus 18.5%.

inference_not_supported: Cure or altered lifelong trajectory.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Ecopipam for Tourette Syndrome: A Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trial
design: Responder-enriched randomized withdrawal.
key_result: Pediatric relapse hazard ratio 0.47.
uncertainty: Enrichment; short follow-up; small adult subgroup.
inference_not_supported: Disease modification, universal response, or regulatory approval.
retrieval_status: PubMed abstract inspected; publication dates and indexed publisher passages verified.

title: A double-blind, sham-controlled, trial of home-administered rhythmic 10-Hz median nerve stimulation for the reduction of tics, and suppression of the urge-to-tic, in individuals with Tourette syndrome and chronic tic disorder
design: Four-week three-group randomized trial.
key_result: Active treatment outperformed sham on tic-score reduction.
uncertainty: Short-term outcome; developer involvement.
inference_not_supported: Cure or proven entrainment mechanism.

key_result: Both patterns helped; no demonstrated post-stimulation persistence.
uncertainty: Short experiment; placebo not excluded.
inference_not_supported: Rhythmic entrainment uniquely explains benefit.
retrieval_status: PubMed abstract inspected.

title: Brain-heart coupling in tourette syndrome: a precision functional mapping study of discordant siblings.
reviewer: dot; single-assistant extraction, not independent clinical peer review

correction_retraction_check.result: No linked CommentsCorrections notice in the retrieved PubMed XML; focused 1-9 October entry-date correction/retraction query returned zero records.

design: Small observational precision-functional-mapping pilot; repeated resting fMRI and concurrent pulse recordings in two TS-discordant sibling pairs.
population: Children with Tourette syndrome and unaffected siblings; published aggregate study description only.
comparator: Unaffected siblings; within-participant repeated physiological/network measurements.
intervention_exposure: No treatment intervention; pulse-derived RMSSD and time-varying functional connectivity.
outcomes: Two targeted sets of autonomic-network coupling analyses; independent preregistration not verified.
followup: Repeated scanning sessions; no sustained-remission or treatment-withdrawal follow-up.
key_result: Individual autonomic-network association patterns differed; evidence is descriptive and hypothesis-generating.
uncertainty: Only four independent participants; repeated windows are dependent. Tics were not independently annotated, respiration was unmeasured, and clinical heterogeneity limits TS-specific inference.
inference_not_supported: An autonomic signal precedes or causes tics; a validated tic predictor, remission mechanism, treatment effect or cure.
adverse_events: Clinical safety was not established; adverse-event extraction not performed for this non-treatment study.
attrition: Participant recruitment/exclusion flow not fully extracted; repeated-window quality control does not establish participant-level retention.
funding: Kavli Institute for Brain and Mind postdoctoral award, Tourette Association of America and NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program, as reported in the paper.
conflicts: Authors report no commercial or financial relationships constituting a potential conflict.
retrieval_status: Publisher full-text methods, results interpretation, limitations and disclosures inspected; no raw-data reanalysis.
related_cohort_note: Participants came from an ongoing UC San Diego precision-functional-mapping study. Overlap with other cohort publications was not resolved.
next_verification_task: Require concurrent tic annotation, respiratory/cardiac controls and held-out temporal prediction before promoting an autonomic-precursor hypothesis; verify participant/cohort independence in later syntheses.

title: ONLINE-TICS: Internet-Delivered Behavioral Treatment for Patients with Chronic Tic Disorders
newness: Historical 2022 publication newly analyzed on 14 October 2026; not new-window evidence.
design: Five-center observer-blind randomized adult trial; self-directed internet CBIT versus online psychoeducation; face-to-face CBIT available at one center.
population: Ages 18–62 with TS/chronic tic disorders; German/internet eligibility; prior behavioral treatment and comorbidity needing primary therapy excluded; not a defined continuously severe adult cohort.
primary_endpoint: Adjusted YGTSS-TTS change at one week after treatment, iCBIT minus control.
key_result: Primary −1.28 points (95% CI −2.58 to 0.01), p=.053. Later exploratory TTS contrasts favor iCBIT at three/six months; impairment and GTS-QOL have distinct timing. Non-inferiority is exploratory because the prespecified primary gate failed.
uncertainty: MAR-dependent mixed model, differential noncompliance, missing visit/outcome-specific denominators, continued platform access, multiple exploratory tests, and ATQ/impairment table–prose discrepancies.
negative_findings: No clear vocal-tic contrast; video-tic V3/V5 intervals include zero. Early urge and life-satisfaction VAS contrasts point unfavorably under standard scoring; trial VAS recoding unverified. CGI-I responder model failed to converge.
safety: 128 incidents, none investigator-attributed to treatment; event counts differ from affected-participant counts; rare harms remain unestablished.
funding_conflicts: BMBF 01KG1421 and EUR 600 advocacy funding; intervention developers among investigators; multiple financial relationships disclosed in paper.
inference_not_supported: Confirmatory primary efficacy/non-inferiority, endpoint surrogacy, joint response, increasing treatment effect, off-treatment durability, disease modification or cure.
reproducible_analysis: Nine-contrast post hoc Holm/Bonferroni sensitivity retains four of six nominally favorable focal contrasts; 33 checks independently reproduced. Not study-wide or confirmatory adjustment.
retrieval_status: Institutional version-of-record PDF text, protocol and official registry API inspected; screenshots failed. Original summaries/aggregates only saved.
correction_retraction_check: No identified correction/retraction in limited exact-identifier/source check; publisher 429 prevents comprehensive clearance.
next_verification_task: Audit adult-dominant Wilhelm 2012 follow-up estimand, response-conditioned participation and boosters; preserve inclusion of ages 16–17 and stop adult-only inference without subgroup data.

title: Randomized Trial of Behavior Therapy for Adults With Tourette Syndrome
publication_date_type: August 2012 journal issue dated August 1; no earlier online-first date verified
newness: Historical 2012 trial analyzed on 15 October 2026; not new-window evidence. PMC author manuscript available 13 September 2013.
design: Three-site masked-assessor randomized ten-week CBIT versus psychoeducation/supportive therapy (PST); response-conditioned follow-up with offered monthly boosters. PST nonresponders could cross to CBIT.
population: Ages 16–69; adult-dominant, not adult-only. TS/chronic tic disorders with at least moderate severity. Six screened with TTS above 30 received panel review; three enrolled and three excluded. Stable medication/comorbidity and English/IQ criteria limit severe/unstable-adult extrapolation.
primary_endpoint: Week-10 tic severity; categorical CGI-I response (1 or 2) separately reported. Impairment is a registry secondary endpoint.
key_result: Published adjusted acute YGTSS-TTS advantage 3.3 points (95% CI 1.4–5.2), p<.001; impairment advantage 3.9 (0.5–7.2), p=.03 without secondary multiplicity adjustment. Six-month CGI-I positive: CBIT 12/15 assessed versus 12/24 all acute responders; PST 1/2 assessed versus 1/4 acute responders.
uncertainty: Continuous model requires a postrandomization visit and MAR; response-selected and incomplete follow-up, booster-inclusive protocol, unverified actual booster attendance, and control crossover prevent a causal all-randomized six-month comparison. No direct original-report follow-up impairment/GTS-QOL effect or adult-only estimate.
negative_findings: Medication/severity moderator nulls do not establish equivalence. Nine of 24 CBIT acute responders and two of four PST responders have unknown follow-up outcomes.
reporting_discrepancies: Abstract PST 4/63(6.4%) conflicts with body/allocation 4/59(6.8%); six-month prose mixes denominators. Reported NNT5 is not reproduced by reciprocal raw CGI risk difference3.1933 (ceiling4). Author-manuscript and final-published impairment/medication percentages differ.
safety: 224 adverse events and three serious events judged unlikely related; tic worsening in four participants per arm. Event totals differ from affected-person counts; rare or long-term harm not excluded.
funding_conflicts: NIMH and Tourette Syndrome Association support; treatment-manual royalties, professional honoraria and other relationships disclosed; sponsor role declared absent.
inference_not_supported: 80% all-randomized six-month response, continuous remission, adult-only efficacy, off-treatment durability, causal long-term superiority, QoL surrogacy, disease modification or cure.
reproducible_analysis: Exact finite-cohort enumeration gives six-month CBIT acute-responder maintenance bounds 50–87.5%, with 62.5% follow-up ascertainment; not confidence intervals. 37 implementation checks plus 49 independent comparison checks passed; output reproduced exactly.
retrieval_status: Final JAMA HTML, PubMed, current official registry API, one readable PMC manuscript fetch and visually inspected PMC flow diagram. No full papers or figures included in deliverables.
correction_retraction_check: None identified in bounded exact-title/DOI searches and inspected PubMed record; not comprehensive clearance.
next_verification_task: Audit same-trial McGuire secondary functioning report (PMID31451122; online2019-08-27, issue2020-09): randomized acute disability/social/family effects versus responder associations and selected follow-up; retain denominators, instrument direction, uncertainty, multiplicity and null findings.

title: Effect of behavior therapy for Tourette's disorder on psychiatric symptoms and functioning in adults
novelty: Historical same-trial secondary report newly audited; not a new 2026 result or independent replication.
design: Secondary exploratory analysis of acute randomized CBIT versus psychoeducation/supportive therapy, postrandomization responder comparisons, and selected CBIT responder/completer follow-up.
population: 122 older adolescents and adults aged 16–69 (mean 31.6), Tourette disorder/chronic motor/chronic vocal tic disorders; clinical stability and other eligibility restrictions. No adult-only or severe-persistent-adult functional estimate verified.

n.outcome_specific_n: Generally unreported. Table 3 parental role has one complete participant and no test; individual values excluded.

comparator: Psychoeducation and supportive therapy, an active attention/support intervention
intervention: Eight CBIT sessions over ten weeks; acute responders offered/planned three monthly boosters, individual attendance unverified.
prespecified_outcomes: Original trial primary acute tic severity. This report describes exploratory ancillary psychiatric and functional outcomes; no prespecified confirmatory functional hierarchy verified.
outcome: SDS disability; FAM-III family functioning; SAS-SR adjustment domains, separately from tic and psychiatric measures. Lower functional scores indicate less disability/maladjustment; SDS total scoring version not fully reconciled.

selected_followup_omnibus.baseline_month6_significance: Not documented by table marker; broader prose should not substitute.

numeric_result.restricted_posthoc_multiplicity: No functional test remains below .05 under separate Holm/Bonferroni families of 12, 12 and 11; these families do not adjust the full study or restore confirmation.

followup: Six months after acute treatment; only acute responders invited, CBIT returnees analyzed; no preserved randomized between-arm comparison.
attrition: 122 randomized, 113 acute analyzed and 105 acute completers differ; outcome-specific denominator/df missing. CBIT follow-up 15 selected returnees; no nonresponder follow-up. Nonsignificant baseline differences do not prove random missingness.
adverse_events: No new systematic adverse-event comparison established by this secondary functioning analysis; psychiatric nonsignificance is not proof of no harm.
risk_of_bias: Exploratory multiplicity, unmasked self-report, missing outcome-specific counts and confidence intervals, postrandomization response conditioning, selected follow-up, no long-term randomized comparator, clinical-stability selection. Figure screening arithmetic and PST follow-up counts conflict.
conflicts_funding: NIMH and TAA/AAN/ABF support. Authors state no work-associated conflicts; detailed consultancy, honoraria and royalties disclosed.
applicability: Mixed older-adolescent/adult clinic sample, not adult-only, representative population or severe-persistent-adult stratum. No pain-specific or GTS-QOL endpoint.
cohort_overlap_status: Same trial as Wilhelm 2012; not independent replication.
claim_supported: No demonstrated acute randomized superiority on the 12 reported functional contrasts. Limited exploratory responder associations and selected within-CBIT follow-up disability changes require distinct interpretation.
claim_not_supported: Equivalence; no clinically important benefit; causal tic-to-function mediation; universal functional improvement; an all-randomized six-month effect; off-treatment durability; remission, disease modification or cure.
retrieval_status: PMC author-manuscript full methods/tables inspected using ordinary HTTP; figure visually inspected; publisher abstract and metadata checked. Final-published full tables not separately inspected. No full paper or n=1 follow-up scores saved.
reviewer: Research assistant extraction plus independent source/numeric audit matching 363 numerical cells and 144 output/marker checks; 13 implementation tests passed. Not clinical peer review.
